findings.text: non-blocking: _merge_stored_rows runs at every return of load (ledger.py:2410, 2422, 2433), so every ledger.load for any project with content now opens the store and json-decodes every stored payload for every project before filtering to one (_indexed_records at run_store.py:649 is not project-scoped). The per-call decode cost the run_ids repair removed is drawn once per stored row per load, on a path every reader in the repository uses, rather than once per station tick.

non-blocking: the replaced read opened the store with sqlite mode=ro and swallowed OSError/sqlite3.Error into an empty answer; the landed read opens RunStore(path), whose __init__ makes the parent directory and whose _create() executes the auxiliary schema and any pending migration, so a read path now writes and a locked, read-only or damaged store raises out of ledger.load instead of degrading to the document answer that is still available.

non-blocking: the ledger reaches the store's private RunStore._indexed_records from outside the owning module. The store exposes records() (which excludes the archive, run_store.py:781) and durable_rows() (which drops the wide detail, run_store.py:840), so no public read answers a project's hot and retired records with their detail; the reuse is correct but the owner should gain that public accessor rather than the private method being called across the boundary.

non-blocking: the head arm's dot is labelled 'head 1f3094e35ae4: 76 passed', while the log the evidence cites records that 76-passed arm at 3eee72acf081 (logs/after-suite.log first line) and the fragment's arm table names 07d166b0f6 for the same 76 passes. Three revisions are attached to one measurement, so a reader cannot tell which commit the 76-passed figure belongs to; the log's revision is the only one backed by a recorded run.

justifications.durability: tests/test_every_ledger_question_reads_the_store.py:238 reddens when run_ids decodes a payload and :241 reddens when one document hides the store's rows, both shown red in logs/negative-control-store.log; the archive read is guarded by :262 (a dropped include_archive loses the retired id) and :300 by the delete-and-rebuild equality.
justifications.evidence: the gate does measure the done_when (tests/test_every_ledger_question_reads_the_store.py:183-300, logs/after-suite.log 76 passed EXIT=0, logs/base-arm.log 58 passed EXIT=0) but the same 76 passes are attributed to three different revisions across logs/after-suite.log:1, the fragment table and docs/figures/.../source-precedence.py:106.
justifications.fit: reckon/ledger.py:2262 calls another module's private RunStore._indexed_records and :2261 opens a write-mode store on a read path; the added names and local-import style otherwise follow the module (ledger.py:2249).
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/ledger.py:2263 makes every reader that returns through load see the store's rows, ledger.py:1156 unions the store's membership into run_ids, and reckon/crew/open_run_index.py:339 stops a store-backed project being cached as empty.
justifications.reuse: reckon/ledger.py:2262 reads through the store's own record read and :2277 through run_store.indexed_run_ids, so the duplicated SQL and the copied archive-path helper the previous review found are gone; the owner is used, though not extended with a public accessor.
justifications.scope_discipline: every changed path is a declared write path or the figure directory the repair advice explicitly granted; the change carries nothing the goal does not imply.
